text.p: Italian debt markets managed to hold in positive territory despite seeing their neighbours in the red following U.S. data which stoked concerns about the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates.
"The markets are pretty nervous. After data from the U.S. t-bonds broke down and dragged Btps with them," said one broker in London.

June Btp futures on LIFFE held above support at 127.00 and traded 25 basis points up on the day at 127.38 in late business. The February 2007 Btp closed six basis points up at 94.28 with a yield of 7.72 percent with a spread of 177 bps over Germany.
Brokers said the Italian market was shifting its focus to fundamentals after this week's bout of political uncertainty. "They seem to have reached some short term equilibrium," one broker said.

Economists said the market should now be starting to think about the possibility of the Bank of Italy lower interest rates towards the end of the month or in May, with preliminary April inflation data from 11 sample cities due later in the month.
This expectation, which depends on the strength of the lira, should be a supporting factor for the coming weeks.

On the political front, Prime Minister Romano Prodi, patching up his tattered coalition, told parliament ahead of a confidence vote on Saturday that he would brook no dissent from hard left communist allies.
"Other episodes like that which put this country's international image at risk are unacceptable," he said.
